regions.name: flow_near_wake
regions.why: Create the missing off-body near-wake box so the separated-shear-layer / bluff-body wake envelope is covered. Bounds are the flow_requirement:near_wake envelope padded by ~0.01 m so the float32 bounds (0.3499999940/1.0499999821/+-0.9799999833/+-0.4899999917) are strictly contained. Level 2 gives 0.04375 m, half the 0.0875 m prior (= exactly level 1), leaving a factor-2 margin for the native p95 span statistic (tolerance 1.5) instead of a knife-edge equality. Level 2 stays coarser than surface level 3, so no surface/layer/quality setting changes and the surface -> wake -> background grading is preserved. Volume 0.72*1.98*1.00 = 1.43 m^3, ~1.7e4 cells. This is an envelope prior, not a measured shear-layer thickness.

regions.name: flow_far_wake
regions.why: Cover the downstream velocity-deficit/shear transport envelope, padded ~0.01-0.02 m beyond the float32 bounds (1.0499999821/2.4499999583/+-1.2599999785/+-0.6299999893). The prior span 0.175 m is EXACTLY the uniform background cell (grading 1.0), so leaving it unboxed relies on an equality that any stricter native comparison or transition cell would break; level 1 = 0.0875 m supplies a factor-2 margin at ~6.9e3 cells. The upstream face overlaps the near-wake box by 0.02 m so maximum level wins and no coarse slot appears between the two envelopes. Kept deliberately at one increment (the scenario states coarser far-wake bounds cost), not refined to surface level.

advisor.hypothesis: The 0.84 layer coverage is a corner/feature-angle extrusion failure at the two streamwise rims (|Y| = 0.70) of the cylinder/end-cap crease, not underresolution. Measured mid-body (|Y|<0.5, dihedral p50 2.8 deg, 0% of edges above feature_angle 60 deg) has 100% of area at the full 7 layers; the deficit regions have a 90 deg dihedral (p95) and 44-50% of adjacent edges above the 60 deg layer featureAngle, and only 42-60% of the local area reaching 5 layers with ~10-15% of the area stuck at 1-2 layers. So snappy is suppressing extrusion across the rim while the global surface size (0.021875 m) is unchanged and adequate there. The layer mover cannot be the cause of the deficit: native log shows "Extruding 11756/11793 faces (99.69%)", 0 faces removed and 0 thickness-ratio truncations, so the shortfall is the per-point featureAngle suppression, not a mover clamp. Remedy: raise layer feature_angle above the 90 deg rim, shorten the requested stack (n_surface_layers 6) so the stack/medial-distance ratio stays low, increase normal and thickness smoothing so rim displacements redistribute, and re-enable the (currently disabled, absolute-height) warped-face guard. Round 1's local_refine to level 4 at the rim only added cells and left coverage at 0.84: refining surface cells at a crease does not create layer space, and the region's level-4 box also destabilised the transition (max_skew 2.85), so the box is removed.
advisor.expected_change: Body-area fraction with >=5 actual layers should rise from 0.8408 to >=0.90, with the fraction at 1-2 layers in the rim bands (y ~ +-0.59..0.74) dropping from ~10-15% toward <5%. Cell count should stay near 250k (n_surface_layers 6 with expansion_ratio 1.1 gives first height 0.0010702 m and stack ~0.0082 m). Mid-body coverage must remain 1.00. Uncertainty: snappy's corner handling may still suppress extrusion over part of the 90 deg crease; if coverage remains below 0.90 the next lever is n_outer_iter=2 (slice-wise growth, not a retry) or a geometry-level crease treatment, not more surface cells.
counterevidence: Mid-body band |Y|<0.5 has coverage_5plus = 1.00 and 0% of edges above the 60 deg layer featureAngle, so the global surface size and first height already extrude correctly away from the crease; the failure is localised, not a global resolution deficit.

native_layer_mechanism_log shows 99.69% face extrusion and 0 removed faces with 0 thickness-ratio truncations, so the mover reported no local clamp; the mechanism is per-point featureAngle suppression at the rim.

query_region at the rim shows finite_fluid_gap_fraction 0 and directional_outward_hit_distance finite_fraction 0, which does NOT prove absent gaps (rays are directional); the local layer space therefore cannot be quantified from these rays, so no cell-across-stack count is claimed.
Round 1 already added a level-4 box at the rim and coverage only moved 0.797 -> 0.841 while max_skew rose to 2.85; a second surface refinement at the same crease has no measured causal basis.
alternatives: Keep n_surface_layers = 7 but raise feature_angle to 130 only: preserves y+ target but keeps the larger stack/medial ratio and the round-1 churn; rejected as first option.
Switch mesh_shrinker to displacementMotionSolver: the v2412 torus ablation shows the motion solver alone left 1.74% adequate coverage, so a shrinker swap is not a general repair.
Set n_grow = 1: propagates NON-EXTRUSION to neighbours, which reduces coverage; used only if isolated-point artifacts reappear.

actions.why: Round 1's level-4 box sits exactly on the rim layer deficit (measured layer_shortfall:0 / layer_shortfall:1) and did not fix coverage; it only raised max_skew from 0.51 to 2.85 and added ~68k cells. Finer surface cells at a crease do not create medial layer space, so remove the box and let the layer-side fix act. The declared scenario boxes flow_near_wake/flow_far_wake are not touched, so both flow_requirement:near_wake and flow_requirement:far_wake native coverages stay 1.0.
actions.name: repair_0

actions.why: Measured rim dihedral p95 = 90 deg and 44-50% of adjacent rim edges above the current layer featureAngle 60 deg, while the mid-body (p50 ~2.8 deg) already extrudes at 100% coverage with the same global surface size. Raising feature_angle to 120 lets the crease extrude instead of being suppressed; the v2412 cube ablation shows featureAngle 130 gives 100% area with >=5 layers for both shrinkers. n_surface_layers is dropped to 6 to shorten the stack and keep the stack/medial ratio low at the rim (absolute first height 0.0010702 m is unchanged, so the flat-plate y+ planning estimate stays 50). expansion_ratio is relaxed to 1.1 to reduce the outer-layer thickness at the crease; n_smooth_thickness and n_smooth_normals are raised so the rim displacement is redistributed rather than collapsing. max_face_thickness_ratio is set to 0.6 to re-enable the warped-face extrusion guard (inactive under absolute heights; not a first-height clamp). n_buffer_cells_no_extrude stays 0 because adding it zeroes displacement on the adjacent ring. n_outer_iter stays 1 and n_grow stays 0 (a non-extrusion propagation would cost coverage). This is a corner/feature treatment, NOT an underresolution or transition defect.

The rim crease that suppresses extrusion is also the region of the transition/concave artifacts (concaveCells:10 with 1057 cells, concaveFaces:2/3/5 up to |Y| 0.93, concaveCells:11/concaveFaces:4 labelled snap_artifact) and of the failed boundary native self-intersection check. Increasing patch smoothing and feature-snap iterations while keeping snap explicit (implicit false) improves the snapped rim surface without loosening any quality gate, and jointly supports the wider layer feature_angle by giving the extruder a cleaner crease. Tolerance stays 2.0 so no additional cell insertion scale change is introduced at the same stage.
